canonical_definition:
What it is. Across the surveyed papers, TinyStories is most commonly described as a synthetic dataset of short, simple stories, often children's stories, generated by large language models. The prevailing framing is as a small, tractable corpus for training and evaluating small or medium-scale models, while still posing text-generation challenges such as coherence and narrative structure.

What it is claimed to measure. Papers link TinyStories to 2 behavioral indicators and no constructs. The prevailing use is to measure text generation, with papers using it to train or evaluate models that generate text, while a smaller line of work uses it to measure story generation through story continuation.

Space of uses. Most papers position TinyStories as a practical training and evaluation corpus, including uses in next-token prediction, story continuation, and generation from unseen story prefixes and suffixes; some descriptions also emphasize that its small size makes training and aggregating N-gram statistics computationally efficient. A smaller line of work uses it alongside Children Stories or ROCStories, and another use is to probe character choices as a content planning attribute.
